sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Git interview questions cover the version control system every developer touches daily — the difference between merge and rebase (and when to use each), interactive rebase for cleaning history, git bisect for finding the commit that broke a test, cherry-pick vs merge for backporting, resolving merge conflicts, Git hooks for code quality, monorepo vs polyrepo trade-offs, GitFlow vs trunk-based development, and the production scenarios interviewers love ("someone committed a secret to git — what now?"). For Maven/Gradle build-tool questions, see the Java Build Tools page.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Git is **a content-addressable file system + a DAG of commits**.

- **Commit** = tree + parent(s) + author + message.
- **Branch** = a movable pointer to a commit.
- **Rebase** rewrites history; **merge** preserves it. Use rebase locally, merge for the shared trunk.
- **Bisect** finds the bad commit in O(log n).
- **Hooks** + CI gates keep the trunk green.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
The interview surface for this module breaks into these focus areas:

- **Code quality gates** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Comparisons** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Git internals** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Git workflows** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Scenario-based** — applied questions tying multiple topics together. Drill these *last*, after the fundamentals are sharp.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Force-push to shared branch** = destroy work; never on main.
- **Rebase vs merge** — rebase your feature branch, merge the PR.
- **Cherry-pick** — single commit across branches; good for backports.
- **Reflog** is the parachute — almost nothing in Git is truly lost.
- **Trunk-based vs GitFlow** — TBD wins for CD; GitFlow for release-train shops.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"My team works trunk-based with short-lived branches, rebases before push, merges via PR, and uses `git bisect` to find regressions. We never force-push the trunk and protect it with required checks + signed commits."*
